resolution: CONVERGED at pass 3. Trust-page audit (Phase B), 2026-08-30. Drafted and fixed in an Opus session; each hostile pass an independent Sonnet subagent told to re-derive every number itself rather than trust the generated site-facts sheet. PASS 1 BLOCK: three errors, all checkable in a minute against the corpus. Two of the 68 enacted bills show the text as introduced rather than enrolled; the claim that a non-enacted bill shows 'whatever the newest posted version is' is false for a large share of them; and the long-summary count was an artefact of a naive sentence splitter that read 'D.C. Official Code' as five sentence ends. PASS 2 BLOCK: the staleness figure was still overstated (73 where the answer is 69) because the generator could not read a version code out of a non-bracket GPO header, and the summary count was off by one because the abbreviation mask was case-sensitive and missed 'sec.'. Both were generator bugs and both are fixed; the ledger also carried a row auditing five named legal defenses the draft does not name. PASS 3 PASS: no errors. The verifier re-implemented the bill-text header parser from scratch, reproduced 69 of 151 and 2 of 68 exactly including the affected bill ids, and independently re-derived every other figure. Two cosmetic ledger defects fixed after that pass: a registered source no claim cited, and a title field that had drifted from the page's own <title>.
notes: WHAT CHANGED FROM THE LIVE PAGE. The coverage overclaim - 'the site tracks all 119th Congress legislation with active floor action or significant co-sponsorship' - was contradicted by the site's own analysis-skip list, which excludes 23 CRA disapproval resolutions that reach the floor by design, and by methodology.html, which said the opposite in the site's own voice. Two live pages disagreeing about the site's own coverage. The replacement names the contradicting category rather than hedging. 'Full bill text - the actual enrolled bill' was true of 68 of 219 bills; the page now says which, says what the other 151 show, and discloses that stored text can lag the newest posted version because an already-analysed bill is not automatically re-fetched - re-fetching it without re-analysing would leave the prose describing a document the page is not showing. 'The two or three most significant things' (real range 1 to 9, and 'significant' is a word the drafting rules ban) and 'one to three sentences' (real range 1 to 14) are now the measured distributions. Three unsourced characterisations removed: that the manual research process is 'effectively inaccessible', that top lines are 'the facts journalists tend to underreport', and that political-strategy coverage is 'available from dozens of sources'. OPEN, FLAGGED FOR JAMES: the version lag itself. 69 of 151 non-enacted bills and 2 of 68 enacted ones are showing older text than Congress.gov now lists. That is the banked flag-version-drift hole, and closing it means re-fetching AND re-analysing those bills, not just re-fetching.
